questions.question: What is another name for the service line?
questions.explanation: The trailer service air line is also called the control line or signal line.

questions.question: When coupling a trailer, what should you do?

options.text: Connect the matching glad hands together.
Connect any glad hands to any other glad hands.
Connect only one set of glad hands.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connect the matching glad hands together.
questions.explanation: When coupling, match the glad hands correctly. They are often color-coded to help. Blue is for service lines and red is for emergency lines.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, the air compressor must build a minimum of ____ in both systems.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air brake system, wait for the air compressor to reach at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: When you need to make an emergency stop, you should:

options.text: Lock the wheels and skid to a stop.
Keep your vehicle in a straight line while stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your vehicle in a straight line while stopping.
questions.explanation: In an emergency stop, use controlled braking or stab braking. Keep your vehicle going straight while braking, but stay ready to turn if needed.

questions.question: A broken exhaust system can:

options.text: Let poisonous fumes into the cabin.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let poisonous fumes into the cabin.
questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system can let poisonous fumes into the cab or sleeper. Check your exhaust system for loose, broken, or missing parts.

questions.question: What is the average driver's reaction time?
questions.explanation: Average reaction time is between 3/4 second and 1 second. At 55 mph, you travel about 61 feet in that time.

questions.question: Backing with a trailer is dangerous because:

options.text: You cannot see what is behind the trailer.
There may be extra weight in the front.
Trailers cannot be driven in reverse.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see what is behind the trailer.
questions.explanation: Backing is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. Only back up if absolutely necessary.

questions.question: When inspecting coupling equipment, the air lines should not:

options.text: Be connected to the glad hands.

questions.explanation: Check that all coupling parts work correctly. Air lines should be connected to the right glad hands with no leaks. They should be secure but have some slack for turning.

questions.question: Why is the road most slippery right when rain starts?

options.text: Water mixes with grease and oil, making the road slippery.
Drivers forget where the windshield wiper lever is.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water mixes with grease and oil, making the road slippery.
questions.explanation: When rain first starts, the water mixes with oil and grease on the road. This creates a slippery surface before the rain washes these materials away.

questions.question: Talking on a hands-free phone while driving:

options.text: Only distracts the driver if speaking.

questions.explanation: Hands-free phones are safer than hand-held phones, but they still mentally distract drivers. Talking takes focus away from driving.

questions.question: What happens if you unlock the pintle hook before removing the dolly from under the rear trailer?

options.text: The tow bar may fly up.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tow bar may fly up.
questions.explanation: Always remove the dolly from under the rear trailer before unlocking the pintle hook. If you don't, the tow bar can fly up and cause serious injury.

questions.question: What was the purpose of front brake limiting valves?

options.text: Prevent the front tires from skidding.
Prevent the front tires from overheating.
Remove uncertainty when applying the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent the front tires from skidding.
questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have front brake limiting valves to reduce the risk of front wheel skidding. Research has shown these devices are not needed. If your vehicle has one, leave it in the "normal" position.

questions.question: Which type of vehicle is most likely to experience the "crack-the-whip" effect?
questions.explanation: Double and triple combinations are most likely to roll over due to the "crack-the-whip" effect.

questions.question: How should you set the front brake limiting valve for normal stopping power?

options.text: Set the control to the off position.
Keep the control at the halfway mark.

questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have a front brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings. These were designed to limit brake pressure on slippery roads. Studies show this is not necessary. If your vehicle has one, keep it in the "normal" position.

questions.question: What does heavy steering often indicate?
questions.explanation: Heavy steering usually means one of your front tires has failed. If your steering feels different, safely exit the road and check your tires right away.

questions.question: What should a driver make sure of regarding the truck's load?

options.text: The cargo is mostly in the front of the trailer.

questions.explanation: Proper loading is essential for safe truck operation. Bad loading affects how the truck handles and can damage it. It can also cause cargo to fall and injure or kill people.

questions.question: Are freeway off-ramps safe for trucks?

options.text: Should not be used by trucks.
Should be used only if following another vehicle.

questions.explanation: Freeway on- and off-ramps have slopes and curves that can be dangerous for trucks. Speed limits posted for cars may be too fast for large or heavily-loaded trucks.

questions.question: When backing a trailer, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: Turn the top of the steering wheel in the direction you want the trailer to go.
Turn the top of the steering wheel in the direction opposite of where you want the trailer to go.
It depends on where the trailer is being backed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the top of the steering wheel in the direction opposite of where you want the trailer to go.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, turn the steering wheel in the opposite direction of where you want the trailer to go. Once the trailer starts turning, switch the steering wheel direction to follow the trailer.

questions.question: What should you do when backing a truck?

options.text: Only use the side mirrors on the driver's side of the vehicle.

questions.explanation: When backing a truck, always use mirrors on both sides of the vehicle. Have someone help you whenever you can.

questions.question: In a double or triple combination, which trailer should be directly behind the cab?
questions.explanation: In a combination, place the heaviest loaded trailer closest to the tractor. Place the lightest trailer in the rear.
